item.title: [7] Crystal electric field excitations and spin dynamics in the spin-orbit coupled distorted honeycomb magnet BiErGeO5
item.description:
Last authors: D. T. Adroja, Gøran J. Nilsen, M. D. Le, and R. Nath

Authors: S. Mohanty, S. Guchhait, S. S. Islam, Surya P. Patra, M. P. Saravanan, J. A. Krieger, T. J. Hicken, H. Luetkens, D. T. Adroja, Gøran J. Nilsen, M. D. Le, and R. Nath

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Interesting neutron scattering study on a spin-orbit coupled magnetic material.

Tags: #neutronscattering #spin-orbitcoupling #magnetism

Abstract: Author(s): S. Mohanty, S. Guchhait, S. S. Islam, Surya P. Patra, M. P. Saravanan, J. A. Krieger, T. J. Hicken, H. Luetkens, D. T. Adroja, Gøran J. Nilsen, M. D. Le, and R. Nath Here, the authors report the magnetic properties, crystal electric field excitations, and spin dynamics of a distorted honeycomb magnet BiErGeO 5 . Inelastic neutron scattering and μSR experiments reveal the effect of crystal electric field leading to a Kramers doublet ground state and anisotropic interactions. Despite an anomaly at T N ≃ 0.4 K in heat capacity, μSR measurements rule out a magnetic long-range order, and instead suggest persistent spin fluctuations down to 30 mK, highlighting unconventional magnetism in this spin-orbit coupled honeycomb system. [Phys. Rev. B 113, 214452] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026

item.title: [8] Gap structure and phase diagram of twisted bilayer cuprates from a microscopic perspective
item.description:
Last authors: Laura Fanfarillo, P. J. Hirschfeld

Authors: Siddhant Panda, Andreas Kreisel, Laura Fanfarillo, P. J. Hirschfeld

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Relates to cuprates and time-reversal symmetry breaking in moiré junctions.

Tags: #cuprate #superconductivity #moiré

Abstract: Author(s): Siddhant Panda, Andreas Kreisel, Laura Fanfarillo, and P. J. Hirschfeld Twisted cuprate Josephson junctions have been proposed as candidate platforms for superconducting states that break time-reversal symmetry. However, experiments report conflicting signatures. Here, the authors show that this variability can arise from microscopic parameters: the systematic exploration of the phase diagram reveals that twist angle θ, filling, and interlayer tunneling strength stabilize distinct competing superconducting states. The results clarify how differences between devices can determine whether time-reversal symmetry breaking appears. [Phys. Rev. B 113, 224523] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026

item.description:

Authors: Anna Fancelli, Matías G. Gonzalez, Subhankar Khatua, et al.

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Neutron scattering relevant magnetic study; provides testable predictions for magnetic materials.

Tags: #neutronscattering #magnetism #theory

Abstract: Author(s): Anna Fancelli, Matías G. Gonzalez, Subhankar Khatua, Bella Lake, Michel J. P. Gingras, Jeffrey G. Rau, and Johannes Reuther Here, the authors reveal a general mechanism by which soft quartic spin modes in isotropic spiral magnets generate a fluctuation-induced spin-wave gap. Unlike conventional spin waves from harmonic modes, the gap in these systems grows with temperature according to a characteristic power law. The results extend the theory of soft-mode dynamics and pseudo-Goldstone modes and provide experimentally testable predictions for neutron scattering studies of magnetic materials that do not rely on fine-tuned ground-state degeneracies. [Phys. Rev. B 113, L220411] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026
